# Add state-aware affordability filtering for storyline options

## Summary

Extend `getStorylineOptions` (or add a companion state-aware accessor) that filters out unaffordable options based on `cost` fields. Store the presented/available option list on `PendingEventChoice` so indexing and save/load remain stable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Affordability filter.** `getAffordableOptions(state, event)` returns options where `cost` is affordable (coins and/or reputation gates checked). Options with no cost are always included.
- **Pending choice stores presented list.** `PendingEventChoice` gains an optional `presentedOptions: StorylineOption[]` field populated at choice-draw time.
- **Filtering is stable.** The presented list is computed once at draw and does not change during the pending choice period.
- **Backwards compatible.** Events with no cost-gated options return the same list as before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `getAffordableOptions()`, update `createPendingStorylineChoice()` to populate `presentedOptions`.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `presentedOptions` to `PendingEventChoice`.

## Deliverables

- New/pure function `getAffordableOptions`.
- `createPendingStorylineChoice` populates `presentedOptions`.
- Unit tests for affordability filter.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — deterministic filtering.
data.title: Add affordability filtering to getStorylineOptions

# Deduct cost and apply extra effects during storyline option resolution

## Summary

At resolution time (`resolveStorylineOption` / `resolveEventOption`), deduct the option's `cost` from the player's resources and apply any `extraEffect` independently of the `effectPolicy`. This is the core gameplay change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Cost deduction.** When an affordable option is selected, its `cost.coins` (if set) and `cost.reputation` (if set) are deducted from `state.resourceBank`.
- **Extra effect application.** Any `extraEffect` is applied after cost deduction, independently of `effectPolicy`. Both can coexist (e.g. accept + pay cost + apply extra).
- **Log messages.** Activity log reflects cost deduction and extra effects.
- **Loss checks.** If deduction drops coins or reputation to zero, normal loss checks fire.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `cost` or `extraEffect` behave identically to pre-change.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `resolveStorylineOption` applies cost + extra effect.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` logging updated.

## Deliverables

- Updated `resolveStorylineOption` and `resolveEventOption`.
- Updated log messages.
- Unit tests for cost/extra effect application.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — straightforward resource mutation.
data.title: Implement cost deduction and extra effects at resolution

# Resolve conditional successors at option resolution time

## Summary

When resolving an option, evaluate `conditionalSuccessors` in order — the first matching rule wins. Fall back to the option's existing `successorId` when no conditions match. This enables branching based on game state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Conditional evaluation.** `conditionalSuccessors` are evaluated sequentially; the first rule whose `{ field, op, value }` matches current `state.resourceBank.{field}` determines the pushed card ID.
- **Fallback.** When no conditions match, the option's `successorId` is used.
- **All boundary cases tested.** Above/below threshold, equality boundary (`==`), and no-match fallback.
- **Successor-card push.** The matched successor is pushed via `pushChainCard` as before.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `conditionalSuccessors` push `successorId` as before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — Update `resolveStorylineOption` to evaluate conditional successors.

## Deliverables

- Conditional successor evaluation logic.
- Unit tests for each boundary/fallback case.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNYFJT006PKLC (cost deduction and extra effects).
- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — pure predicate evaluation.

# Update resolveEventOption to use the stored presented option list

## Summary

`resolveEventOption` in `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` currently indexes into `getStorylineOptions(event)` (the full list). Update it to use `pending.presentedOptions` (the affordability-filtered list) so the option index stored at draw time maps correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Index into presented list.** `resolveEventOption` resolves using `pending.presentedOptions[optionIndex]` instead of `getStorylineOptions(event)[optionIndex]`.
- **Fallback to full list.** When `presentedOptions` is null/empty, fall back to `getStorylineOptions(event)`.
- **Transcript stability.** The transcript records the chosen option label from the presented list.
- **Backwards compatible.** Legacy events without `presentedOptions` behave identically.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` uses `pending.presentedOptions`.

## Deliverables

- Updated `resolveEventOption`.
- Unit tests confirming index stability.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed.

# Update AI policy to select only among presented/affordable options

## Summary

`decideEventChoice` in `MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` currently returns `'accept' | 'reject'` and reasons about `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`. Generalise it to select from the presented option list, accounting for cost and extra-effect deltas when projecting outcomes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AI selects from presented options.** The AI considers only options in the presented list (already filtered by affordability).
- **Cost-aware projection.** When projecting outcomes, the AI accounts for `cost` and `extraEffect` in addition to `effectPolicy` effects.
- **Regression harness passes.** The Monte Carlo and regression harnesses run to completion without AI stalls or invalid selections.
- **Backwards compatible.** For legacy binary-choice events, AI behaviour is identical to before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice` generalised for multi-way affordability-aware selection.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolvePendingEventChoice` wiring updated.

- Regression/Monte Carlo harness tests green.

# Extend storyline validator and schema to cover cost, extraEffect, conditionalSuccessors

## Summary

Update the static validator (`src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) and the JSON schema (`schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`) to understand and validate the new optional fields. Reject invalid data (negative costs, unknown fields/ops, dangling conditional successors).

- **Cost validation.** Reject negative or zero costs.
- **Condition validation.** Reject conditions with unknown `field` or `op`; reject non-numeric `value`.
- **Extra effect validation.** Reject negative extra effect values.
- **Conditional successor validation.** Reject dangling conditional successors.

# Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version

## Problem statement

`npm run build` silently compiles against whatever commit happens to be checked out in the `./core` submodule (currently `dc4ec0ce`, v0.1.21-3-gdc4ec0ce), and nothing ever updates it. Dev builds can therefore skew from the latest engine without anyone noticing, while release builds are not reproducible because nothing records which engine commit they were built against.

## Users

- **Game developer (internal)** — wants dev builds to always compose the latest Tableau Card Engine so behaviour is tested against current engine code. User story: "As a game developer, I want `npm run build` to pull the engine's latest remote HEAD, so my builds reflect current engine behaviour without manual submodule surgery."
- **Release operator (maintainer)** — wants deterministic, reproducible release builds. User story: "As a release operator, I want release builds to compile against exactly the engine SHA recorded in a committed pin file, so a release can be reproduced bit-for-bit from source."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run build` (and `npm run build:electron`) runs an `engine:sync` step before compiling: `git submodule update --remote core` fetches the latest remote HEAD of whatever branch `core` tracks and checks it out. The build fails loudly (never clobbers) if `./core` has uncommitted changes.
2. `npm run build:release` runs an `engine:verify` step instead: it reads the committed pin file `configs/engine-pin.json` (engine SHA), checks out exactly that SHA, and fails the build if the pinned SHA differs from the remote-resolved target or contains local modifications.
3. `configs/engine-pin.json` holds a single `sha` field (e.g. `{"sha": "dc4ec0c..."}`) and is written only by the release process (alongside the version bump) — never by dev builds.
4. The `engine:sync` / `engine:verify` npm scripts are independently invocable (`npm run engine:sync`, `npm run engine:verify`) and covered by unit tests for the dirty-state guard and pin-mismatch failure paths.
5. The build-script template change is made in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (engine repo) and main-street is re-scaffolded so a future re-scaffold does not clobber the change. Full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related documentation (docs/dev, README/DEPLOYMENT as applicable) is updated.

## Constraints

- **No CI beyond npm builds** — there is no separate CI pipeline; `npm run build` is the verification vehicle. Release pinning is enforced at tag/merge time only, not by a CI job.
- **Scaffold ownership** — `package.json` scripts and `vite.config.ts` in main-street are scaffolded from `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (engine repo). The dev/release script change must land in that template, then main-street is re-scaffolded; editing only the generated copy gets clobbered.
- **`git submodule update --remote` must never overwrite dirty submodule state** — fail loudly instead.
- Core's remote default branch is `main`; the submodule may be checked out detached or tracking a branch — sync must behave correctly for either.

## Existing state

- `.gitmodules` declares `core` → `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine.git`.
- `package.json` has `build: "tsc --noEmit && vite build"` and `build:electron`; no `build:release`, no engine sync/verify steps.
- Submodule currently at `dc4ec0ce` (v0.1.21-3-gdc4ec0ce), never auto-updated.

## Desired change

- Add `engine:sync` (dev auto-update + dirty guard), `engine:verify` (pin check + exact checkout), and `build:release` scripts; wire `engine:sync` into `build`/`build:electron` and `engine:verify` into `build:release`.
- Introduce `configs/engine-pin.json` owned solely by the release process.
- Update the scaffold template in the engine repo (`core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) so generated game repos get the same scripts; re-scaffold main-street.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — new `engine:sync`, `engine:verify`, `build:release` scripts; `build` / `build:electron` wiring.
- `scripts-*` (generated via `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) — new engine sync/verify script that the npm scripts invoke; located in the engine repo template and re-scaffolded into main-street.
- `configs/engine-pin.json` — new committed pin file (`{"sha": "..."}`).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — engine-repo template to update so re-scaffolds carry the new behaviour.
- `vite.config.ts` — generated; verify re-scaffold preserves any needed changes (no manual edits expected).
- `docs/dev/*` — build/release documentation to reflect dev/release split.

## Related work

- MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV — "Core scaffold template Pages base" (completed): precedent for the cross-repo process of editing the core scaffold template and re-scaffolding this repo; the implementation consideration in this item mirrors it.
- MS-0MV5928XV0007X1J — "Cross-repo: core pack-asset byte seam + submodule bump" (completed): precedent for bumping the `core` submodule pointer as part of main-street work.
- MS-0MV76P7BN00164RF — "Toneforge should be off by default" (completed): documents the cross-repo submodule-bump discipline.
- MS-0MUQ1KXAS003FJ42 — "Ship web-based copy of Main Street (GitHub Pages)" (completed): release/deployment pipeline context.
- MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV — "Load the committed ToneForge runtime synth module" (completed): submodule-bump precedent.
- MS-0MV16VZWP001OUNR — "Full-suite verification & release readiness" (completed): release-gating precedent.
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` / `core/AGENTS.md` — engine-repo docs to update when the scaffold template changes.
- MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED risk note: a bad `engine:sync` could land a broken engine commit in dev builds; mitigation is the loud-failure dirty guard and the pin/verify split.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: auto-sync lands a broken engine commit.** Dev builds silently move to a newer engine that may be red on its own suite. Mitigation: `engine:sync` is loud about what it changed and dirty-state guard prevents clobbering; the pinned release path is the safety net.
- **Risk: dirty `./core` submodule.** `git submodule update --remote` refuses when uncommitted changes exist; we must surface that as an explicit build failure, not a silent skip.
- **Risk: network/remote dependence.** Dev builds now require reachable GitHub at build time; offline builds fall back to current checkout with a warning (assumption — confirm behaviour during implementation).
- **Risk: scope creep** — pin-file metadata (tags, dates), CI jobs, or Steam/Electron packaging integration are out of scope; record as linked work items if needed.
- **Assumption:** core's tracking branch may change; sync follows whatever branch `core` tracks (operator answer Q2-A), which matches the submodule's configured remote branch.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What should the key testable outcomes be?" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "B — dev/release paths both produce correct results, dirty-state detection prevents accidental commits, `engine:sync` / `engine:verify` independently callable (noting: no CI outside npm builds)". Source: intake round 1.
- Q2: "How aggressive should engine:sync be?" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "A — always fetch latest remote HEAD of whatever branch core tracks". Source: intake round 1.
- Q3: "CI impact?" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "C — keep CI as-is; release pinning is enforced at tag/merge time only". Source: intake round 1.
- Q4: "Pin file schema?" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "A — `{"sha": "..."}` only". Source: intake round 1.
- Q5: "Scaffold template changes?" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "A — update in the core repo's scaffold template, then re-scaffold main-street". Source: intake round 1.
data.title: Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version

# Feature 3 Tests: projection parity

## Summary
Tests asserting AI/projection value equals actual payout for the dynamic synergy in both single-player and competitive modes, including piggyback projection and animation attribution.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Test single-player: `projectEventCoinDelta` == actual `resolveEvent` payout for Food-placement scenario.
2. Test competitive: `computeCompetitiveEventValue` == per-owner `computeOwnerEventDeltas` payout.
3. Piggyback projection path equals expected dynamic reward.
4. `scoreEventAction` value consistent with the dynamic payout.
5. Animation attribution (`MainStreetAdjacencyScoring`) marks the dynamic-match slots. Full suite passes.

# Feature 3: AI/projection parity

## Summary
Mirror the dynamic synergy in AI value/projection paths so projections never diverge from the actual payout: `projectEventCoinDelta`, `countOwnSynergyMatches` callers, `scoreEventAction`, `computeCompetitiveEventValue`, `MainStreetAdjacencyScoring` animation attribution, and piggyback projections.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `projectEventCoinDelta` for `evt-grand-opening` counts grid cards sharing the placed synergies (per current state), not static Commerce.
2. Competitive AI path: `computeCompetitiveEventValue` and any `scoreEventAction` usage compute the dynamic (per-owner) value.
3. Piggyback reward projections (competitive grand-opening is piggybackable) reflect the dynamic payout.
4. `MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` per-slot animation attribution flags the same dynamic-match slots.
5. A shared resolver/helper is used by all paths so projection and payout can never diverge (single source of truth).

## Dependencies
Depends on Feature 2 resolution (MS-0MVCS7LIA003J2SM).
data.title: Feature 3: AI/projection parity
